subject: Startups
title: Who Owns the Code
description: Learn Who Owns the Code in one minute.

hook.text: A co-founder quits and claims they own the codebase because they wrote it before the company was formed.

buildup.text: IP assignment agreements transfer all work-related intellectual property from individuals to the company.

discovery.text: Without signed IP assignments, the company may not actually own its own product. Investors check this in due diligence.

twist.text: Code written at a previous employer might belong to them. Using it in your startup can trigger devastating lawsuits.

climax.text: Every founder, contractor, and employee should sign an IP assignment on day one. No exceptions. No handshake deals.

punchline.text: If you didn't sign for it, you might not own it.

quiz.question: Why do investors check IP assignments during due diligence?
options: To confirm the company actually owns its product
